text:
olivia_acme: Hey team — we exported our daily usage CSV and the rows around Mar 15/16 are split between two days. Our org timezone is America/Los_Angeles, but the CSV looks like it used UTC midnight. Billing is wrong for that day, can you confirm? Ticket #INC-2042

tara_support: Sorry about that, olivia. Can you paste the export command/endpoint you used and a short snippet of the CSV (first 10 lines)? Also which org id so we can repro.

olivia_acme: Org: acme-corp (org_987). Exported from Console -> Billing -> Exports -> Daily usage CSV (applied date range Mar 14–17). Here is a tiny excerpt: 

```
date,org_id,tokens,requests
2026-03-15,org_987,12450,92
2026-03-16,org_987,230,3
2026-03-16,org_987,11820,89
```

The UI dashboard shows almost all traffic on 2026-03-15 (PDT) but the CSV split a small chunk into 03-16. We think the midnight boundary used for bucketing is UTC.

tara_support: thanks. Reproduced locally for org_987 with your export range. Quick check: the console UI header says "Daily usage (America/Los_Angeles)" but the exported CSV header is unlabeled and the date column appears to be UTC. Looking into backend logs now. @maya_analytics can you check the aggregation job timestamps?

maya_analytics: I pulled the daily-aggregator logs for org_987. The aggregator writes two timestamps: ingest_ts (UTC when event arrived) and billing_day (string). For this org billing_day was computed correctly for the daily dashboard via tenant.timezone, e.g. billing_day = '2026-03-15' for most events. But the export worker uses a separate path that re-derives day from ingest_ts without passing tenant.timezone. Looks like a missing TZ param in exports pipeline.

ricardo_sre: Confirmed root cause: exports service call stack (exports-worker -> daily-sum-service) calls compute_day_bucket(event.ingest_ts) instead of compute_day_bucket(event.ingest_ts, tenant.timezone). This only surfaces when tenant.timezone != UTC and around DST boundaries or cross-midnight windows. Minimal repro: run the export job with --org=org_987 and set system TZ=UTC vs America/Los_Angeles to observe the shift.

olivia_acme: Ugh. Is there a workaround while you ship a fix? Our finance team needs corrected CSV for invoicing.

tara_support: Workaround: use the Console's "Download per-usage JSON" (not CSV) — those records include explicit billing_day that respects org timezone. Or run the export endpoint with query param ?tz=America/Los_Angeles — internal note: we can surface this param in UI quickly. I'll attach a corrected CSV and escalate for re-run.

maya_analytics: Patch idea: change exports-worker line 142 from:

```
// current
const day = computeDayBucket(event.ingest_ts);
```

to:

```
// proposed
const tz = tenant.timezone || 'UTC';
const day = computeDayBucket(event.ingest_ts, { tz });
```

Add unit tests for DST boundary cases and an integration test that runs export-worker against sample events with tenant.timezone set.

ricardo_sre: I'll pick up the PR. Plan: small patch + unit tests, canary to staging, run export on org_987 sample, then deploy to prod during low-traffic window (overnight PDT). Rollback easy by reverting computeDayBucket param change. Pushing a draft PR now.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary/staging -> 2026-03-18 03:00 PDT; prod -> 2026-03-18 09:30 PDT (manual approval required). CI results pending.

olivia_acme: Thanks all. Can you re-run the export for org_987 and send corrected CSV to olivia@acme.com? We need it by EOD PDT.

tara_support: Will do. I've queued an immediate re-run using the JSON->CSV conversion (corrects billing_day). Sending now and will follow up after the fix is deployed. Keeping this thread updated. :thumbsup:
